questions.stem: Which of the following describes why voice communication matters, according to PAM 6-0102 (0134)?
questions.key: It remains the bedrock of tactical communication despite computer networks and satellite communication
distractors: It has replaced computer networks as the main means of tactical data exchange
It is the only means that works beyond line of sight
It is the least vulnerable means to interception and jamming
questions.explanation: PAM 6-0102 (0134) states that despite computer networks and satellite communication, voice communication remains the bedrock of tactical communication.
why: The manual says voice remains the bedrock; it does not say voice replaced data networks.
HF can reach over the horizon, and other means exist; voice is not the only one that does.
Voice radio is exposed to interception and jamming, which is why the plan includes protective measures.

questions.stem: It is what PAM 6-00 (0205) calls the voice of command, because it carries the commander's information down to lower commands and units.
questions.explanation: PAM 6-00 (0205) calls the communications system the voice of command because it carries the commander's information to lower commands and units.
why: The signal estimate is an examination of factors affecting the signal mission.
The CEOI gives operating instructions (what to do); it is not called the voice of command.
The vigilance net is a net reserved for emergency and exigent situations.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the vigilance net?
questions.key: A net reserved for emergency and exigent situations and used in joint operations, which is less secure and open to eavesdropping
distractors: A separate net treated as unclassified and unsecured that connects the many entities in a disaster response
A net on which each nation keeps its own sovereign network, with defined points of integration
A net reserved for routine administrative traffic between a unit headquarters and its elements
questions.explanation: PAM 6-0102 (0316) describes the vigilance net as reserved for emergency and exigent situations and used in joint operations; because it is less secure, users rely on ciphertext and double talk.
why: This describes the disaster response net, which is kept separate from the Army's secured operational net.
This describes the coalition arrangement of sovereign national networks.
The vigilance net is for emergencies, not routine administrative traffic.

questions.stem: Two handheld radios loaded with a unit's operational frequencies are captured in an ambush. This describes which recovery concern the plan must address (PAM 6-0102 0311)?
questions.explanation: PAM 6-0102 (0311d) says radios may fall into enemy hands, so the plan must include procedures to change frequencies quickly.
why: Interrupted connectivity concerns faults or damaged equipment, not captured radios.
A cyberattack needs the cyber response team; captured radios are a frequency compromise.
Jamming is disruption of the net, not capture of equipment holding frequencies.

questions.stem: A manual sample plan names a Harris handheld VHF radio as the primary means, a Harris manpack radio as the alternate and a messenger as the last resort. In PACE, the messenger is which level?
questions.explanation: PAM 6-0102 (0312a) sample plan: handheld VHF primary, manpack alternate, and a messenger as the emergency means.
why: Contingency is the level between the alternate and the emergency means.
The primary is the handheld radio.
The alternate is the manpack radio.

questions.stem: A signal team must visit brigades, battalions and companies to repair UHF commercial radios, program radios and give refresher training. This describes which facility?
questions.key: Signal mobile maintenance and repair team (SMMART)
distractors: Deployable brigade tactical operations center system (DBTOCS)
questions.explanation: The SMMART does level 1 to 2 repairs of UHF commercial radios, radio programming and refresher training, and visits brigades, battalions and companies.
why: The SMTF is the fixed facility that repairs tactical HF and VHF radios up to level 3.
DBTOCS extends fixed communications to brigades; it is not a maintenance team.
The CNR system is a radio network, not a maintenance facility.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines fixed communications in the voice handout?
questions.key: BONTEX, PANET, the AFP fixed communications system and DBTOCS, which extends fixed communications to brigades
distractors: HF, VHF and UHF radios and combat net radio using radio over IP and ad-hoc networks
Commercial video-conferencing, cellular phones and satellite phones
Messengers, liaison officers and pre-arranged visual signals
questions.explanation: PAM 6-0102 (0133) lists the fixed means as BONTEX, PANET, the AFP fixed communications system, with DBTOCS extending fixed communications to brigades.
why: These are the tactical (mobile) means.
These are the special purpose means, used with prudence and within COMSEC policy.
These are emergency fallbacks, not a category of communication means.

questions.stem: It is the band covering 3 to 30 MHz, used for long-distance ground communication, with a 20 W manpack fielded.
questions.explanation: PAM 6-00 (glossary and 0514) gives HF/SSB as 3 to 30 MHz for long-distance ground communication, with a 20 W manpack fielded.
why: VHF/FM is 30 to 80 MHz, for short-distance communication, with a 5 W handheld fielded.
UHF/FM is 403 to 433 MHz, for internal communications.
Commercial cellular is a special purpose means, not an HF band.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three categories of communications means in PAM 6-0102 (0132 to 0135)?
questions.explanation: Communications are fixed, mobile (tactical) and special purpose.
why: Strategic is a level of command, not a category of means.
Primary, alternate and contingency are PACE levels.
Commercial services fall under special purpose; they are not a separate category.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three resource areas the planner keeps an up-to-date chart of (PAM 6-0102 0306 to 0309)?
questions.explanation: The planner charts C4S equipment (0307), personnel (0308) and funds (0309).
why: Facilities are support facilities of the fixed system, not a charted resource area.
Frequencies are managed through the CEOI and spectrum management, not charted as a resource area.
Training status is part of the personnel chart, not a separate area, and equipment is omitted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the sources of voice requirements in PAM 6-0102 (0305)?
distractors: Guidance from higher, subordinate and adjacent headquarters
questions.explanation: The sources are the commander's guidance, staff guidance, higher, subordinate and adjacent headquarters, SOPs, and the CEOI and CESI. Enemy signal capabilities is the E in METAL, a factor of the estimate.
why: SOPs are a listed source.
The CEOI and CESI are a listed source.
Guidance from higher, subordinate and adjacent headquarters is a listed source.

questions.stem: Which means is the primary means on the strategic-to-operational headquarters link (PAM 6-00 0406)?
questions.explanation: The 0406 table gives the AFP FCS, with the Army providing drop and insert to major camps, as primary between strategic and operational headquarters. HF/SSB is secondary and commercial landline is tertiary.
why: HF/SSB is the secondary means on this link.
Commercial landline is the tertiary means on this link.
Mobile communications are a tertiary option only if funds permit.
